articles.title: New Dark Project Ransomware Group Offers Hackers 80% Commission to Expand Cyberattacks
articles.summary:
A ransomware group called Dark Project is recruiting criminal partners with an offer of 80% of proceeds from successful attacks, pairing generous commissions with a platform for managing extortion. First observed in June 2026, the financially motivated operation combines data theft, file encryption, and public leak threats to pressure organizations into paying. The group’s published […]

articles.title: Microsoft Warns Fake Game Downloads Are Secretly Monetizing Windows PCs
articles.summary:
Fake game downloads and cracked software installers are turning Windows PCs into money-making tools for campaign operators. Microsoft has warned that deceptive installation packages quietly deliver software that shares internet bandwidth, runs distributed-computing workloads, or installs unwanted utilities, often without users understanding what they have agreed to install. The campaign targets people searching for free […]

The post Microsoft Warns Fake Game Downloads Are Secretly Monetizing Windows PCs appeared first on Cyber Security News.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Claude Code Reportedly Leaks User Email Addresses Through HTTP User-Agent Headers
articles.summary:
Anthropic’s Claude Code is facing privacy concerns after a user reported that the AI coding tool sent their email address to third-party websites through HTTP User-Agent headers during web searches, without permission. The report raises questions about how coding agents handle personal data while carrying out routine tasks. GitHub user taylor-edwards filed issue #107757 on […]

The post Anthropic’s Claude Code Reportedly Leaks User Email Addresses Through HTTP User-Agent Headers appeared first on Cyber Security News.

articles.title: Hackers Launch 240,000 Exploit Attempts WordPress Core Flaw Enabling Remote Code Execution
articles.summary:
Hackers have launched more than 240,000 exploit attempts against a WordPress Core vulnerability that can allow attackers to run malicious code without logging in. According to the supplied Wordfence report, attacks began on October 28, 2026, the same day WordPress released a security update addressing the flaw. Tracked as CVE-2026-119977, the vulnerability carries a high […]

articles.title: Mirax Android RAT Hijacks Phones Through Streaming-App Ads to Steal Banking Credentials and Drain Accounts
articles.summary:
An Android banking malware campaign is turning streaming-app advertisements into a route for stealing credentials and draining accounts. Mirax, the remote access trojan lets criminals watch infected phones, intercept security codes, and operate banking apps directly from victims’ devices. Thousands of Android phones belonging to retail banking customers across the Middle East, Turkey, and Africa […]

articles.title: ARTEX AI Agents Steal 190,000 Gaming Credentials and Hundreds of Apple Code-Signing Certificates
articles.summary:
Cybercriminals are now using ARTEX, an AI-powered penetration testing platform, to break into websites with almost no human input. In the cases studied, the AI agents stole more than 190,000 gaming credentials and over 300 Apple code-signing certificates. Only three of those certificates still worked. ARTEX was built as an open-source tool to help security […]

The post ARTEX AI Agents Steal 190,000 Gaming Credentials and Hundreds of Apple Code-Signing Certificates appeared first on Cyber Security News.

articles.title: Hackers Use ARTEX AI to Find GitHub Secrets and Steal Azure Key Vault Data in Just 5 Minutes
articles.summary:
Hackers are using the ARTEX AI framework to find exposed credentials on GitHub and turn them into access to cloud systems. In one observed case, an AI agent moved from searching public repositories for application secrets to stealing data from Azure Key Vault in just five minutes, showing how quickly a coding mistake can become […]

The post Hackers Use ARTEX AI to Find GitHub Secrets and Steal Azure Key Vault Data in Just 5 Minutes appeared first on Cyber Security News.

articles.title: Storm-2603 Hackers Exploit SharePoint ToolShell Flaws to Hide Fileless Backdoor and Launch Ransomware Attack
articles.summary:
A China-linked threat group tracked as Storm-2603 has used the SharePoint ToolShell flaws to plant a backdoor that never touches the disk. The group then tried to run Warlock ransomware on the same network. The break-in hit an on-premises SharePoint server and ended with a ransomware launch that security software blocked. ToolShell is the name […]

The post Storm-2603 Hackers Exploit SharePoint ToolShell Flaws to Hide Fileless Backdoor and Launch Ransomware Attack appeared first on Cyber Security News.

articles.title: ARTEX AI Hacking Framework Found on 1,465 Public Servers, Some Hosting Cyberattack Tools
articles.summary:
Security researchers have found ARTEX, an AI-powered penetration-testing framework, exposed on 1,465 internet-facing hosts. Some servers also hosted command-and-control tools, phishing software, and exploit files, showing how automated security-testing platforms are appearing alongside established attack infrastructure. The findings offer defenders a view of these environments, including files operators left publicly accessible. The count does not […]

The post ARTEX AI Hacking Framework Found on 1,465 Public Servers, Some Hosting Cyberattack Tools appeared first on Cyber Security News.

articles.title: Claude Dispatch Flaw Lets Malicious Browser Extensions Run Code on Connected Computers
articles.summary:
A flaw in Anthropic’s Claude Dispatch let a malicious browser extension run commands on a computer via Claude Desktop. That computer could even be a different machine signed into the same Claude account. Researcher Gal Weizman of Forever Security named the technique ThisBash and published the findings on November 4, 2026. Anthropic plans to retire […]

The post Claude Dispatch Flaw Lets Malicious Browser Extensions Run Code on Connected Computers appeared first on Cyber Security News.
